transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Your Name]. Thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to take up too much of your time. I just... I've been having a bit of a hard time lately at work. I'm a gambling surveillance officer, and it's usually fine, but recently, things have been a little strange. 

I guess what finally scared me enough to come in—and please tell me if this sounds crazy, I'm just trying to be honest—is that during the quiet stretches in the surveillance room, I've been hearing things. I hear voices coming through the monitor speakers. They say things like, "You missed it, Ruth," or "People are going to get hurt because of you." The thing is... every channel is muted. And when I ask my coworkers, no one else hears anything. I'm sure it's just stress or exhaustion, right? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out.
Ruth, have you felt like others might be watching you or talking about you, even when there's no clear reason to think so?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I've felt like that. I mean, besides what I mentioned about the... the voices on the monitors, I don't feel like real people are watching me or whispering about me. I try really hard to be a good coworker and get along with everyone, so I'd like to think they wouldn't have any reason to talk behind my back. 

I know it's a little ironic since my whole job is watching other people, but... no, I haven't noticed anything like that happening to me personally. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions okay... I just really want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you what you need to figure this out.
Ruth, besides hearing voices on the monitors, have you noticed any other unusual experiences—like seeing things that others don't, or feeling sensations on your skin that don't have a clear cause?

Um, no... no, thankfully. I haven't seen anything out of the ordinary, and my skin feels completely normal. It's really just... just the things I mentioned with the audio on the monitors. 

I hope that's a good sign? I mean, I really don't want to make things more complicated for you to figure out, so I'm sort of glad I don't have anything else to add for that one. But no, I haven't noticed any other strange sensations or visions or anything like that at all. Does that... does that help rule some things out for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Ruth, do you ever feel like the voices or anything else you've experienced might be part of something larger, like someone trying to send you a message or trying to harm you in some way?

Oh, um... no, not at all. I don't feel like anyone is out to get me or trying to hurt me. It's really just... just the weird audio thing at work. I don't think it's part of some big plot or anything like that. I'm sure it's just my brain playing tricks on me because I've been so stressed and tired lately. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly, me even coming in for this, but I just wanted to be safe. I really hope I'm not wasting your time with all of this. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing. Does that make sense? I'm not trying to make a big deal out of nothing, I promise.
Ruth, have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?

Um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? I feel kind of embarrassed even admitting it, because I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or feeling sorry for myself. But... yeah, most days, it feels like this... this heavy, gray mood just sort of settles over me before I even get out of bed in the morning. 

And, um... sometimes I'll be sitting in my car before my shift starts, and I'll just start tearing up. Over absolutely nothing, really—just seeing the casino lights can make me cry lately. I know that sounds so ridiculous. I always try to wipe my face and put on a smile before I walk in, so no one else has to deal with it or worry about me. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything... I'm still doing my best to be productive and do a good job. Is it normal to get overly emotional like that when you're just really worn out? I'm hoping it's just exhaustion, but I wanted to be honest with you since you asked.
Ruth, have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, don’t interest you as much anymore?

Um... well... I guess I have been a little less social lately. I hope that's okay to admit. I just... I don't want you to think I'm antisocial or pushing people away on purpose. 

But, yeah, I used to really look forward to things. Like, I'd go to salsa class, or play softball, and I loved building PCs. I even used to have people over for board games all the time. But lately... I don't know, I just sort of ignore the texts when they come in. I just sit at home, and it feels like... like none of it can really reach me anymore, if that makes sense? 

I know I should be making more of an effort, and I'm really trying not to let my friends down. I just haven't had the energy for it. Is that... is that something you see a lot when people are just really stressed out from work? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Ruth, how long have you been feeling this way, with the heavy mood and losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, it's been a little while now. I'd say... maybe about four months? 

It kind of started right around the time they promoted me to the lead casino surveillance role. Which, I know, I should be really grateful for! It's a good opportunity, and I really don't want to sound unappreciative of the promotion. I'm trying really hard to step up and do a good job for them. 

I just... I think maybe the transition has been a bit more overwhelming than I expected. That's probably a normal reaction to taking on more responsibility, right? I'm hoping it's just an adjustment period and I'll snap out of it soon. I really don't want to be a burden or let anyone down at work.
Ruth, have you noticed that you’ve been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

Um... yes, I guess I have been feeling pretty tired lately. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy, because I really do try to push through it. I don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off. 

But... it's just that, even if I've been in bed all night, doing really basic things just feels so incredibly hard right now. Like, even just doing my rounds walking the parking garage at work, or coming home and trying to cook a simple dinner... it feels like I'm dragging myself around. It's almost like I'm wearing this heavy, weighted vest that I just never get to take off. 

I know everyone gets tired, and I'm probably just not managing my time or my stamina as well as I should be. I'm really trying to do better with it. Is it normal to feel that kind of exhaustion when you're just adjusting to a new role? I just want to make sure I'm not complaining about something everyone else just deals with normally.

Ruth, have you ever felt like things are happening that others don’t seem to notice or understand, like maybe events around you have special meaning just for you, or that you’re receiving special messages from somewhere?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think so? I hope I'm understanding your question right. I definitely don't think I'm receiving special messages or anything like that. That sounds like something that would be... well, a lot more serious than what I'm dealing with, right? 

I just go to work, watch the monitors, and come home. Everything is pretty normal, just... tiring. I really try to stay grounded and focused on my job. I'm not imagining things or anything. I hope that's the right answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. Is it okay that I don't have anything like that going on?
Ruth, have you noticed that you don't get any pleasure or satisfaction from things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Um... yeah, I guess that's been happening a bit, too. I really hate to admit it, because I know how important it is to stay active and keep up with friends. I don't want to seem like I'm just shutting people out or being a bad friend. 

But... well, I used to really look forward to things. Like, I'd go to salsa class, play in a softball league, or even just stay in and build PCs... I used to have people over for board games all the time. It was fun! But lately... I don't know, I just kind of ignore the texts when they ask me to hang out. I just sit at home, and it's like... like none of it can even reach me anymore. 

I know I should be making more of an effort, and I'm really sorry if that sounds like I'm just giving up. I'm trying to be better about replying to people. Do you think that's just part of being so tired from the new job? I really hope I'm not doing something wrong by taking a step back from all of that right now.
Ruth, would you say that your mood has been consistently down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Um... I really want to say no, because I try so hard to keep a positive attitude. I know how important it is to be professional, and I really don't want to come across like I'm just feeling sorry for myself or complaining. But... yes, I guess it has been pretty consistent lately. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, but most days... I feel like this heavy, gray mood just settles over me before I even get out of bed. And sometimes, well... I can actually tear up in my car before my shift, over absolutely nothing. Just seeing the casino lights as I pull into the lot is enough to make me start crying. 

I always wipe my eyes and pull it together before I go inside and clock in, I promise! I would never let it affect my job or make anyone else uncomfortable. I just... I don't know why I'm being so sensitive. Do you think that's just a normal reaction to being so exhausted all the time? I really hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Ruth, have you ever had times when your thoughts felt unusually disorganized, or when you struggled to make sense of things that others seem to understand easily?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try to keep my thoughts very orderly. With my job in surveillance, watching the casino floor on the monitors... I really have to stay sharp and keep track of everything going on. If I couldn't make sense of things, I'd be letting my team down, and I would absolutely hate to be a burden like that. 

My thoughts are pretty clear, honestly. Maybe just a little slow sometimes because I'm so tired, like we talked about, but definitely not disorganized or confused. I hope I'm understanding your question right? I just want to make sure I'm not missing what you're asking... is that the kind of answer you need?

Ruth, besides the voices you’ve heard on the monitors, have you ever had any experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t, even when there was no proof or it didn’t make sense?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I know that mentioning the things on the monitors earlier probably makes me sound a little... well, I really hope you don't think I'm completely out of touch with reality. I'm honestly so embarrassed about that as it is, and I really hate to even talk about it. 

But besides that, no, I don't have any strange beliefs or anything like that. I really pride myself on being very practical and level-headed. In my line of work, you have to rely strictly on the facts and what you can actually prove, you know? I would never want to be the kind of person who just makes things up or stubbornly believes things that don't make sense. I promise I'm still very grounded in the real world. 

Does that... does that make sense? I just want to reassure you that I'm thinking clearly. I hope that's the right way to answer your question.
Ruth, have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, don’t interest you as much anymore?

Um... well, I really try to stay active and engaged, I promise I do. I know it's so important to have a good work-life balance and to be a good friend. I don't want to sound like I'm just giving up or being lazy... but, well, yes, I guess things have changed a bit lately.

I used to really look forward to things. Like, I'd go to salsa class, or play softball, and I loved building PCs. I even used to have people over for board games all the time. I really enjoyed being the host and making sure everyone had a good time. 

But lately... I don't know, it's a little shameful to admit, but I just... I kind of ignore the texts when people invite me out. I just sit at home, and it feels like... like none of it can even reach me anymore. I just don't have the energy to be good company right now, and I'd hate to bring everyone else down with my mood. 

Is that... is that normal when you're feeling this tired? I really hope I'm not coming across as antisocial or ungrateful for my friends. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even the parts I'm not very proud of. Is this the kind of information you need?
Ruth, have you ever had times when you felt like your thoughts were jumping all over the place, or when you couldn’t organize your ideas properly, even outside of feeling tired?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I really try to keep my thoughts very organized, like I mentioned before. I know it's so important to be clear-headed, especially with my job. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my grip on things or that I can't put a sentence together. 

I mean, sometimes when I'm really exhausted, I might lose my train of thought for a second, but it's never like my ideas are just jumping around out of control. I always make sure to stay focused and present. I'd be so embarrassed if I couldn't even organize my own thoughts, you know? I really try my best to stay on top of things. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way. I promise I'm really trying to be as clear as possible.
Ruth, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I know it's really important to eat right and take care of yourself, and I always try to make sure I'm getting enough nutrition. I don't want to sound like I'm neglecting my health or anything like that. 

I guess I haven't been quite as hungry as usual, but I still make sure to eat my meals. I definitely haven't lost any noticeable amount of weight or anything drastic like that. I really try to keep everything steady and normal. I'd hate for you to think I'm just wasting away or not taking care of myself. 

Is that... does that answer what you're asking? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Ruth, have you had days when you felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks or more in a row?

Um... well, I mean, I try really hard not to let myself get stuck in a rut like that. I know how important it is to keep a positive attitude and just push through, especially when you're working. I really don't want to come across as someone who just wallows or complains, you know? 

I guess... I mean, I did mention that I haven't been going out as much lately, and I do feel tired... but I wouldn't say it's been like a solid block of two weeks where I'm just completely down every single day. I still get up and go to work, and I try to keep my chin up. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up on everything. 

I really try to find the good in things when I can. Is it okay if it's not exactly two straight weeks? I just want to make sure I'm not exaggerating anything or making it sound worse than it is. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for?
Ruth, would you say that your mood has been consistently down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Um... well, I really try not to let it get to me, you know? I know I have to be alert and professional for my job, and I'd hate for anyone to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all day. I really do try to put on a brave face.

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, and I know you want me to be honest... it has been pretty hard lately. It's like... most days, there's just this heavy, gray kind of mood that just settles right over me. Even before I get out of bed. And it's so silly, but sometimes I'll be in my car before my shift starts, and I'll just start tearing up over absolutely nothing. Like, just seeing the casino lights can make me cry, and I don't even know why. 

I feel so foolish admitting that. I really don't want you to think I'm emotionally unstable or anything. I'm usually much stronger than this. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on, even if it's not very flattering.
